page: Amazon Web Services g5g.metal is a bare-metal server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. The system features 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For graphics and accelerated workloads, it integrates two NVIDIA Turing T4G GPUs with a combined 32 GB of VRAM. It does not include local storage, relying instead on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics are relatively weak, as seen in the single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores, the multi-core capabilities are strong, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 97,247.12. Memory performance is highly efficient for small cached blocks, reaching a read-only bandwidth of 3,787.58 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write operations drop to average levels. The server also exhibits strong performance in software compilation with Clang and ray tracing benchmarks.

This hardware configuration is optimized for graphics-intensive applications, Android game streaming, and multi-threaded ARM-native workloads. It delivers strong performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. However, it is less suited for large-scale language model inference, where text generation speeds for 70B models fall to a poor 2.35 tokens per second. The lack of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.metal is a bare-metal, GPU-accelerated server featuring 64 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory and two NVIDIA Turing T4G GPUs providing 32 GB of total VRAM. The server does not include local storage and operates with a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 97,247.12, and strong small-block cached memory read bandwidth. However, single-core performance and large-model LLM text generation are relatively weak. This server is best suited for graphics-intensive applications, multi-threaded ARM-native workloads, software compilation, and static web serving, offering a specialized hardware profile that balances ARM-based compute density with dedicated GPU acceleration.
